# The Morning He Came Looking

Daniel had always believed that he could handle life on his own.

He was not a bad man.

At least, that was what he told himself.

He went to church. He knew how to pray. He knew many Bible verses. He could sing worship songs with his eyes closed and raise his hands during praise.

If someone asked him whether he believed in God, he would answer without hesitation.

“Yes, I do.”

But believing that God existed was not the same as surrendering his life to Him.

Daniel was a churchgoer, but he lived much of his life like a man who did not know God.

On Sunday, he could sit among believers.

On Monday, he could return to the same sins.

He knew what the Bible said, but he often chose what pleased him.

He wanted God's blessings, but he did not want God's authority.

He wanted God's protection, but he did not want God's correction.

For years, he managed to live that way without thinking too deeply about it.

Until one day, everything began to fall apart.

---

## WHEN LIFE COLLAPSED

First, Daniel lost his job.

He told himself he would find another one quickly.

But weeks became months.

Then a business deal he had invested his savings in collapsed.

The money disappeared almost overnight.

Then came unexpected expenses in his family.

The little he had left began disappearing.

Friends who had once surrounded him became difficult to find.

Phone calls went unanswered.

Promises were forgotten.

Daniel began waking up in the middle of the night with his heart racing.

One night, after staring at the ceiling for hours, he finally got out of bed and knelt beside it.

“God,” he whispered, “I need You.”

It was one of the most honest prayers he had prayed in years.

But after a few moments, his prayer changed.

“Please give me another job.”

“Please provide money.”

“Please protect my family.”

“Please remove this problem.”

“Please restore what I have lost.”

He prayed for a long time.

Then he went to sleep.

The next morning, nothing had changed.

His bills were still there.

His problems were still there.

His fear was still there.

So Daniel prayed again.

And again.

But nothing seemed to change.

---

## THE SEARCH FOR AN ANSWER

Daniel decided that perhaps he had not prayed hard enough.

He began fasting.

He attended prayer meetings.

He went to **prayer mountains with others**, hoping that perhaps the atmosphere of prayer would bring the breakthrough he desperately needed.

He cried.

He pleaded.

He quoted Scripture.

He lifted his hands toward heaven.

He asked God to intervene.

But days passed.

Nothing seemed to happen.

Then someone told him about a man of God.

“He is powerful,” his friend said.

“He knows things about people's lives that nobody else could know.”

“They say miracles happen through his ministry.”

“Go and see him.”

Daniel had already tried everything he knew.

So he went.

---

## THE MEN OF GOD

The man listened to Daniel's story.

Then he looked at him seriously.

“There is something happening in your family,” he said.

Daniel leaned forward.

“What is it?”

The man told him about family covenants.

He spoke about things that might have happened generations before Daniel was born.

He told him that certain spiritual agreements needed to be broken.

Daniel was frightened.

“How do I break them?”

The answer came quickly.

“Give a seed offering.”

Daniel gave.

Nothing changed.

He returned.

Another instruction came.

“Give another seed.”

Daniel gave again.

Still nothing happened.

Someone else told him that perhaps the problem was connected to a relationship he had once had.

Another told him there were consequences connected to sexual relationships he had entered into outside God's will.

Another spoke about covenants he might have made through fornication.

Daniel listened to every explanation.

He was desperate.

He wanted answers.

More importantly, he wanted relief.

So he paid.

He gave.

He followed instructions.

He went from one person to another.

One prophet.

Another prophet.

A prophetess.

Another so-called man of God.

Each seemed to have an explanation.

Each seemed to have an answer.

And almost every answer required something from Daniel.

Sometimes it was called a seed.

Sometimes it was called an offering.

Sometimes it was a special sacrifice.

Sometimes he was told that another prayer session was needed.

Sometimes he was told that another spiritual problem had been discovered.

And Daniel kept paying.

---

## WHEN DESPERATION BECOMES VULNERABILITY

At first, Daniel had savings.

Then the savings became smaller.

Then smaller.

Then almost nothing.

He began selling things in his house.

His television.

His furniture.

Things he had worked years to acquire.

He gave them away in the hope that the next offering would finally unlock his breakthrough.

He was told:

“Your miracle is near.”

So he gave again.

“Your breakthrough is coming.”

So he gave again.

“Do not stop now.”

So he gave what remained.

But his situation did not improve.

Instead, Daniel became poorer.

More frightened.

More confused.

And more desperate.

He had gone looking for help.

But those who claimed to have answers had taken what little he had left.

Some people even took advantage of his fear by sending him to other people who claimed to know hidden things about his life.

Daniel followed them too.

He was desperate enough to try almost anything.

But nothing helped.

He had searched everywhere.

He had prayed.

He had fasted.

He had gone to prayer mountains with others.

He had sought counsel.

He had visited men and women who claimed to speak for God.

He had given offerings.

He had given everything he could.

And still...

Nothing.

---

## THE EMPTY HOUSE

One evening, Daniel sat in his nearly empty house.

There was very little left.

The room looked different.

The things he had once owned were gone.

His money was gone.

His confidence was gone.

His strength was gone.

Even his hope was almost gone.

He sat quietly for a long time.

Then he began to cry.

Not the kind of crying he had done before while asking God for money.

Not the crying of a man demanding a miracle.

This was different.

It was the crying of a man who had finally reached the end of himself.

Daniel looked toward heaven.

“Lord...”

He stopped.

For the first time, he did not know what to ask for.

He had already asked for money.

He had asked for a job.

He had asked for protection.

He had asked for healing.

He had asked for breakthrough.

He had asked for miracles.

Now he had nothing left to ask for.

So he told God the truth.

“Lord, forgive me.”

The room became silent.

“I have been looking everywhere except to You.”

His voice trembled.

“I have wanted Your help, but I have not wanted You.”

He covered his face.

“I have gone to church, but my heart has been far from You.”

“I have called myself a believer, but I have lived like I don't know You.”

“I have continued in things I knew were wrong.”

“I have wanted You to protect me while I refused to obey You.”

Daniel began to weep.

“I have been running from You.”

Then he whispered:

“Lord, I surrender.”

---

## THE PRAYER THAT CHANGED EVERYTHING

Daniel did not ask God for money that night.

He did not ask for a new job.

He did not ask for a miracle.

He simply prayed:

“Jesus, forgive me.”

“Take my life.”

“I cannot save myself.”

“I cannot fix myself.”

“I cannot carry this anymore.”

“I surrender everything to You.”

“Teach me to know You.”

“Teach me to obey You.”

“Deliver me from the things that have held me.”

“Where I have sinned, forgive me.”

“Where I have hurt people, help me make things right.”

“Where I have been deceived, give me wisdom.”

“Where I have trusted men instead of You, forgive me.”

“I want You, Lord.”

“Not just Your blessings.”

“Not just Your protection.”

“Not just Your provision.”

“I want You.”

Then Daniel became quiet.

For several minutes, he simply knelt there.

And something happened inside him.

His circumstances had not changed.

His bank account was still empty.

His problems had not disappeared.

But the burden inside his heart began to lift.

For the first time in a long time, Daniel felt peace.

Not because everything had been solved.

But because he had finally surrendered the person who needed to be changed most.

Himself.

---

## THE MORNING AFTER

The next morning, Daniel woke before sunrise.

For a moment, he forgot about his problems.

Then they came rushing back into his mind.

The debt.

The uncertainty.

The future.

But something was different.

He did not feel alone.

He opened the Bible that had belonged to his grandmother.

As he turned the pages, his eyes fell upon a passage he had read many times before:

> “Through the LORD's mercies we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not. They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness.”

Daniel read the words slowly.

**New every morning.**

He looked through the window.

The sun was beginning to rise.

Yesterday had been filled with failure.

But yesterday was no longer today.

God had given him another morning.

Another opportunity.

Another invitation.

Another chance to walk with Him.

Daniel smiled through his tears.

He finally understood something he had never understood before.

God's mercy was not permission to continue living in sin.

It was God's invitation to come out of sin.

God was not simply interested in fixing Daniel's circumstances.

God wanted Daniel's heart.

---

## THE GARDEN

Daniel remembered the story of Adam and Eve.

God had given them everything they needed.

Yet they disobeyed Him.

When they realized what they had done, they hid.

They covered themselves.

They were ashamed.

But then something remarkable happened.

God came looking for them.

“Where are you?”

God knew where they were.

He knew what they had done.

Yet He called them.

He did not abandon them.

He came looking.

Daniel realized that the same pattern had followed humanity throughout history.

People run.

People hide.

People sin.

People become ashamed.

People try to fix themselves.

People search everywhere for answers.

But God continues calling.

**Where are you?**

Not because He does not know.

But because He wants us to stop hiding.

---

## WHAT DANIEL FINALLY UNDERSTOOD

Daniel eventually understood something that changed the way he saw God.

God was never supposed to be an emergency service.

He was never meant to be someone Daniel remembered only when everything else failed.

God wanted a relationship.

That was the reason He created humanity in the first place.

And when humanity fell, God did not simply turn His back.

He began the work of bringing humanity back to Himself.

The greatest expression of that love came through Jesus Christ.

> “For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life.”

God did not wait for humanity to become perfect.

He came looking for us.

---

## NOT EVERY RELIGIOUS PERSON HAS SURRENDERED

Daniel also learned another difficult lesson.

Going to church does not automatically mean that someone has surrendered to God.

A person can know worship songs and still live far from God.

A person can carry a Bible and still refuse to obey it.

A person can fast for days and still refuse to repent.

A person can attend prayer meetings and still be controlled by sin.

A person can seek miracles while refusing the One who performs them.

Religion can become a hiding place.

But surrender removes the hiding place.

That is why Jesus told the story of the Pharisee and the tax collector.

The Pharisee stood before God speaking about his own goodness.

The tax collector could barely lift his eyes.

He simply prayed:

> “God, be merciful to me, a sinner.”

The tax collector understood what the Pharisee had missed.

God was not looking for a performance.

He was looking for a humble heart.

---

## THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN SEEKING GOD'S HAND AND SEEKING GOD

Daniel began to understand the difference.

There is nothing wrong with asking God for help.

There is nothing wrong with praying for provision.

There is nothing wrong with asking for healing, protection, wisdom, or restoration.

But there is something wrong when we want God's hand without wanting God's heart.

When we want His provision but reject His instructions.

When we want His protection but refuse His correction.

When we want His blessings but refuse His Lordship.

When we want Him to remove the consequences of our choices while refusing to surrender the choices themselves.

Daniel had spent years seeking God's hand.

Now he wanted God's face.

---

## A DIFFERENT KIND OF MIRACLE

Daniel's life did not suddenly become perfect.

He still had consequences to deal with.

He still had debts.

He still had relationships to repair.

He still had to rebuild what had been lost.

But now he did it differently.

He began making things right where he could.

He apologized to people he had hurt.

He stopped certain relationships and practices that had drawn him away from God.

He became accountable.

He learned to pray without bargaining.

He learned to read Scripture not merely to find promises for himself, but to understand the God who had given them.

He learned that repentance was not merely feeling sorry.

It meant turning around.

It meant coming home.

And slowly, his life began to change.

Not because someone had sold him a miracle.

Not because he had discovered a secret formula.

But because he had finally surrendered himself to God.

---

## THE MESSAGE FOR EVERYONE

Daniel's story is not only for churchgoers.

It is for anyone who has ever felt lost.

For the believer who has drifted.

For the person who does not believe.

For the person who has been disappointed by religion.

For the person who has been manipulated by people claiming to speak for God.

For the person who has prayed until they are exhausted.

For the person who has tried everything.

For the person who has reached the point where there seems to be nowhere else to go.

The invitation is still the same:

**Come to God.**

Not because you have earned the right.

Not because you are already perfect.

Not because you have finally solved your life.

Come because He loves you.

Come because Christ has opened the way.

Come because His mercy is still available.

Come because His compassion has not failed.

---

## THE MORNING HE CAME LOOKING

Years later, Daniel would sometimes remember that empty house.

He would remember sitting among the few possessions he had left.

He would remember the money he had lost.

He would remember all the people he had visited looking for answers.

He would remember the offerings he had given.

He would remember the fear.

He would remember the shame.

But most of all, he would remember the night he finally stopped asking God to fix his circumstances and asked Him to transform his heart.

That was the night everything changed.

Looking back, Daniel realized something.

He had spent years searching for God.

But God had been searching for him.

Just as He had searched for Adam.

Just as He had called the tax collector.

Just as He had sent Christ into the world.

God had been calling:

**“Where are you?”**

And when Daniel finally answered,

“I am here, Lord,”

he discovered that God had never stopped loving him.

---

# THE LESSON

You may have run from God.

You may have failed Him.

You may have lived a double life.

You may have gone to church while your heart remained far away.

You may have tried prayer, fasting, religious rituals, advice, money, people, and every possible solution.

You may even have been disappointed by people who claimed to have answers from God.

But do not let the failures of people convince you that God has failed.

And do not let your own failures convince you that God has stopped calling.

There is a difference between **seeking God because you need something from Him** and **seeking God because you need Him**.

God wants more than your emergency prayer.

He wants your heart.

He wants your surrender.

He wants you to know Him.

He wants to lead you out of the things that are destroying you.

He wants to restore the relationship that sin has broken.

And that is why Jesus came.

Not merely to make your earthly life comfortable.

But to reconcile you to God.

So if you are reading this and you feel far from Him, you do not need to wait until you are perfect.

You do not need to clean yourself up first.

You do not need to pretend.

You do not need impressive words.

You can simply come honestly.

**“Lord, have mercy on me.”**

**“Forgive me.”**

**“I surrender.”**

**“I want to know You.”**

**“Take my life.”**

And perhaps, when you finally stop running, you will discover what Daniel discovered:

You were not the one who found God.

**He was the One who came looking for you.**

And tomorrow morning, when the sun rises, remember:

> **His mercies are new every morning.**

Yesterday may have been painful.

Yesterday may have been filled with failure.

Yesterday may have contained mistakes you wish you could undo.

But if God has given you another morning, then His mercy is speaking again.

**Come home.**

**The Father is still calling.**

**The door is still open.**

**And His love has not failed.**

### The End
